# Prompting and In-Context Learning {#sec-prompting}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Chapter status: skeleton.** Port core content from the CME 295-based
workshop material (prompting section); rewrite examples for the
non-CS audience.
:::

**Learning objectives.** After this chapter you can:

- explain in-context learning and why examples in the prompt work at all;
- apply the core prompt patterns: role, structure, few-shot, chain-of-thought;
- design prompts as *specifications*, with output contracts (JSON/schemas);
- run a small prompt A/B test instead of arguing from anecdotes.

The uncomfortable truth of applied LLM work: [the prompt is part of the
model]{.hl}. Treat it like code — versioned, tested, reviewed — not like a
chat message.
